# Data Dictionary — Synthetic COPD Longitudinal Dataset

**This dataset is 100% synthetic**, generated by `generate_dataset.py` for a
course ML/digital-twin demo. It is not real patient data and should never be
described as representing real clinical outcomes — say so explicitly in your
report/viva ("synthetic dataset generated to demonstrate the pipeline").

- 400 synthetic patients, 3–8 visits each, 2,196 total rows
- Visit spacing is irregular (3–12 months) — realistic, not evenly sampled
- Includes deliberate missing values and outliers for a genuine preprocessing step

## Columns

| Column | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | string | Synthetic patient identifier (P0001…P0400) |
| `visit_number` | int | 1 = baseline visit, increases per follow-up |
| `months_since_baseline` | float | Time elapsed since Visit 1 — **the sweep variable for trajectory/simulation** |
| `sex` | M/F | Static |
| `age_at_visit` | float | Age at this visit |
| `gold_stage_baseline` | categorical | Disease severity classification set at baseline (I–IV) |
| `smoking_status_baseline` | never/former/current | Smoking status at Visit 1 |
| `smoking_status_at_visit` | never/former/current | **Can change over time** (cessation events) — this is the field a "quit smoking" what-if scenario flips |
| `pack_years` | float | Smoking exposure, static |
| `activity_level_at_visit` | low/moderate/high | **Can change over time** — the field an "increase activity" what-if scenario flips |
| `bmi` | float | Static |
| `baseline_fev1_liters`, `baseline_fvc_liters`, `baseline_fev1_fvc_ratio` | float | Twin's static identity, fixed at Visit 1 |
| `fev1_liters` | float | **Primary prediction target** — observed lung function at this visit |
| `fvc_liters`, `fev1_fvc_ratio` | float | Observed at this visit |
| `spo2_pct` | float | Blood oxygen saturation; ~4% missing by design |
| `cat_score` | float | COPD Assessment Test (0–40, higher = worse symptoms); ~3% missing by design |
| `exacerbations_this_visit` | int | Count of acute worsening events since last visit |
| `measurement_source` | clinic/home_device | Where the reading was taken |
| `injected_issue` | none/missing_spo2/missing_cat/outlier_fev1 | **Ground truth for grading only — never use as a model input.** Lets you demonstrate "here's what I found and cleaned" with a verifiable answer key. |

## How this maps to the project design

**Digital twin state** = the `baseline_*` columns (fixed identity) + the most
recent visit's time-varying columns (`fev1_liters`, `smoking_status_at_visit`,
`activity_level_at_visit`, etc.) + the visit history list.

**"Add Visit"** = append a new row for that `patient_id` with an incremented
`visit_number` and `months_since_baseline`; the twin's current state becomes
that new row.

**ML prediction target**: train on `fev1_liters` as the label, using
`age_at_visit`, `sex`, `gold_stage_baseline`, `smoking_status_at_visit`,
`pack_years`, `activity_level_at_visit`, `bmi`, `months_since_baseline`,
and `baseline_fev1_liters` as features. (`fvc_liters`, `spo2_pct`, `cat_score`
are downstream *consequences* of FEV1 decline in this simulation, not causes
— don't feed them in as predictors of `fev1_liters` or the model will look
artificially perfect by leaking the answer.)

**Simulation / trajectory**: hold a patient's baseline + current features
fixed, sweep `months_since_baseline` forward (e.g. every 6 months for 3
years), and call `model.predict()` at each step — this generates the curve
directly from the trained model, not from a hardcoded formula.

**What-if scenario**: same sweep, but with `smoking_status_at_visit` or
`activity_level_at_visit` changed for one branch — compare the resulting
curve against the baseline (unchanged) curve.

**Train/test split**: split by `patient_id`, not by row — a patient's
visits are correlated, so putting different visits of the same patient in
both train and test would leak information and inflate your metrics.
